To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we designed a 0.13 μm CMOS chip with 4/10 channels for simultaneous optogenetics and multi-channel electrophysiological (LFP/AP) recording.
we have developed a novel 0.13 μm CMOS SoCs for simultaneous multichannels optogenetics and multiunit electrophysiology.
We present the first 13μm IC with multichannel opto-physiology recording capability for simultaneous in vivo multichannel optical stimulation and electrophyisological brain recording.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the design, fabrication and characterization of an IC for simultaneous optogenetic and electrophysiology recording in freely behaving small laboratory animals, which is the first time this is achieved.

the design and implementation of a CMOS SoC to enable simultaneous multichannel electrophysiological and optogenetic recording in vivo, which is a key enabler for the study of neural circuits in freely behaving laboratory animals.
the development of a novel brain-implant IC that can simultaneously perform multichannel opto- and neuro-stimulation.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
this paper reports a 0.13 μm CMOS SoCs for multichannel opto-electrophysiological recordings in the same device.

the presented chip is the first to combine optogenetics and multi-channel electrophysiological data acquisition in a single chip, and that the chip can be used for simultaneous in vivo recording and stimulation of multiple brain regions.
we report the design, fabrication, and characterization of an integrated circuit for simultaneous multichanel optogenetic stimulation and electrophysiologic recording.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have developed an IC for simultaneous optogenetics and multi-channel electrophysiological signal recording, which is the first of its kind.
this is the first time a CMOS SoC chip is reported to include both multichannel optical stimulation and electropysiological recording capability.
we have developed a 0.13µm CMOS SoIC that can be integrated with a wireless optogenetic device to perform simultaneous multichannel optical stimulation and electropysiological recording.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the proposed chip is capable of simultaneous multichannel electrophysiological and optical stimulation, and is the first chip to achieve such capability.

the proposed chip can be used for the study of neural microcircuits and their modulation by light in freely behaving small laboratory animals, and can also be used to record the activity of a large number of neurons with minimal invasiveness.
the proposed IC can be used to study neural circuits in vivo in a wide variety of brain regions and species, and can be integrated in a wireless platform to enable free-behaving animal experiments.
